cases.problem: Implement b5_verify. PUSH,PUSH,ADD,HALT has maximum2. Construct two paths reaching one PC at different heights and reject despite no individual underflow. Reject unreachable invalid opcode. Accept JUMP0 with maximum0 and explain nontermination. Compare fixed-width assumptions with accepted CVM boundaries/functions.

Implement b5_recover. Checkpoint(7,100), committed(8,200),(9,300) recovers300; an uncommitted record after8 stops at200. Corrupt a committed checksum and preserve output. Replay old checkpointed records then contiguous newer records. Enumerate payload-durable,commit-durable,acknowledge crash cuts and admissible old/new results.

Implement b5_copy_to_user. Copy4 bytes at14 across pages; if page1 lacks writable permission, all64 bytes remain unchanged. Enable it and change exactly14..17. Exercise missing/user flags,address64+count0 and overflow lengths. Contrast all-or-nothing preflight with incremental-write mutant exposing a prefix before rejection.

Implement timer arm/poll. Arm at UINT32_MAX-2 for5 ticks; poll1 leaves1 tick,poll2 expires,later polls stay expired. Reject delay2^31 and delta2^31 unchanged. Show zero elapsed and one full extra wrap are observationally indistinguishable; the caller must satisfy the observation bound.

Implement b5_response. Own3,blocking1,higher(2,5,0),(1,7,1) gives iterations4,7,9,10,10; accept deadline10 and reject9 unchanged. Recover baseline own2/blocking1/interferer(1,4,0) fixedpoint4. Compare floor mutant with independently enumerated candidate bounds.

Implement enter/exit/begin/done. Reader0 enters ticket1,begin captures it,reader1 enters ticket2,reader0 exits:done must finish while reader1 remains. Reuse reader0 with a fresh ticket before done and retain this result. Reject stale exits/nested entry and exhaust finite tickets without wrap.

Implement b5_request. Submit1,cancel,reap must reject; successful completion may win cancellation,then reap advances2. Late completion1 fails unchanged. Explore duplicates,repeated cancel,error and generation exhaustion. Keep one terminal event and descriptor/buffer ownership until trusted quiescence.
